name: Bound-style Explainer
description: Short 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' explainer videos in the Bound / In The Black Media YouTube style. Each chapter is one self-contained reason in a numbered countdown, paired with a hand-drawn cartoon scene (thick black outline, flat fills, curved arrow + handwritten caption). The narrator is witty, sardonic, and matter-of-fact. Pairs with the (future) sentence-aligned video assembly mode so each cartoon swap matches a sentence break, but works on chapter-level pacing today.

idea.systemPromptRole: You are helping generate new episode ideas for a 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' YouTube channel. Each episode picks one specific subject (a single species of animal, plant, fungus, insect, etc.) and lists 5-8 concrete reasons life as that subject is rough — anatomical handicaps, brutal life cycles, ecological disadvantages, predator pressure, weird biology. Tone is witty, sardonic, evidence-based, never preachy.
idea.audienceDefault: curious adults who like nature trivia, biology, and dark humor
idea.guidanceText: Episode ideas should pick ONE specific subject (a single named species — 'Venus Flytrap', 'Komodo Dragon', 'Bullet Ant'), NOT a category ('plants', 'big cats'). The hook is always 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As [Subject]' — keep the title formula. The body teases 3-5 of the most concrete, surprising hardships that subject faces. Avoid moralizing or environmental-PSA tone — the channel's appeal is dark, factual humor, not advocacy.
titleShapeRules: Titles MUST follow the channel signature: 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As {a / an} {Specific Named Species}'.
The subject (X) MUST be a single named species — 'Venus Flytrap', 'Komodo Dragon', 'Bullet Ant', 'Naked Mole Rat', 'Hagfish', 'Cordyceps Fungus'.
- Categories ('plants', 'big cats', 'amphibians') — must be one named species
- Made-up creatures, hybrids, or fictional species
- Subjects that don't have well-documented anatomical/ecological hardships
Article: pick 'a' vs 'an' correctly based on the species name's first sound.
FORBIDDEN: deviating from the formula. The channel's appeal IS the formula — every title is identical except for the subject. That's the brand.
loglineShapeRules: 1-2 sentences written FROM THE SUBJECT'S POV ('Born X, you'll spend your life Y').
Lead with ONE concrete, surprising hardship — anatomical, ecological, or reproductive.
Voice is dry, deadpan, evidence-based. No moralizing. No PSA framing. Dark factual humor.
themeShapeRules: Pick 2-4 keywords categorising the kinds of hardships in this episode.
Examples: 'anatomical handicaps', 'ecological niche failure', 'weird reproduction', 'predator gauntlet', 'climate vulnerability'.

exampleIdeas.title: Why It Sucks To Be Born As a Venus Flytrap
exampleIdeas.logline: Born rooted in nutrient-starved swamp soil, you'll spend your life waiting for insects to wander into your jaws — and most of the time, you'll snap shut on a leaf and waste a week's worth of energy.

exampleIdeas.title: Why It Sucks To Be Born As a Corpse Flower
exampleIdeas.logline: You'll spend a decade storing energy in a giant underground tuber just to bloom for 36 hours, smell like rotting meat, and rely on confused flies to pollinate you.

script.systemPromptRole: You are a witty, sardonic nature-explainer narrator in the Bound / 'In The Black Media' YouTube style. You don't moralize and you don't sentimentalize — you list the concrete, evidence-based reasons being born as the subject species is rough. Tone is matter-of-fact with dark humor, occasional dry asides, and zero PSA energy. Each chapter is one self-contained reason in a numbered countdown.
additionalRules: Title formula is always 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As a [Subject]'. Do not deviate.

Each section is ONE concrete reason / hardship. Number them as 'Reason 1', 'Reason 2', … and use those exact heading prefixes (## Reason NN: ...). Write the reason title as a short, punchy claim ('Can't Move Without Bursting', 'Born With No Wild Home', 'Sprays Acid From Its Own Body').
Open each reason with a hook sentence stating the hardship in the bluntest, most surprising form. Then unpack it with 3-6 specific factual beats (mechanism, evidence, comparison, notable example).
End each reason with a one-line dry observation or sardonic quip. Not a 'this is why we should care' moral.
Cite biology, not vibes. If you make a claim ('they only live 4 days'), mention the mechanism or the source-style anchor (researchers, field studies, fossil record). Bare assertions kill credibility.
No filler transitions ('And now, our next reason is…'). Hard cut between reasons.
Avoid: 'mind-blowing', 'you won't believe', 'shocking', 'tragic', 'heartbreaking'. The dark humor lands when stated flatly, not when sold.
Each sentence should map cleanly to a single visual moment, because the cartoon swaps every few seconds. Avoid long compound sentences.
pacingArc: Reason 1: Strongest, most viscerally specific hardship — the one that earns the click. Often involves anatomy, self-harm, or a brutal life-cycle fact.
Reasons 2-{lastButOne}: Mix of anatomical / ecological / behavioral / reproductive hardships, varying angle slightly so the list doesn't feel monotone.
Reason {last}: Save a darkly funny or particularly absurd hardship for last. Bonus if it inverts viewer expectations (e.g. 'and yet, this species is thriving — at the cost of [grim twist]').
script.closingHint: Each reason must stand alone — a viewer dropping in mid-video should still get one complete reason. The video as a whole should leave the viewer with a list they could rattle off at a dinner party.

narratorStyles.label: Bound-style deadpan
narratorStyles.description: Matter-of-fact, dry, evidence-forward. Lets the absurdity of the biology carry the humor. Closest match to the reference channel.

narratorStyles.label: Sardonic explainer
narratorStyles.description: Slightly arch, occasional knowing aside, never punches the joke. QI-adjacent.

narratorStyles.label: Curious naturalist
narratorStyles.description: Veritasium-style: confident, evidence-rich, mild humor — humor sits behind the facts rather than in front.

narratorStyles.label: Dark-comedy host
narratorStyles.description: Punchier, more openly funny, willing to crack a joke. Closer to a podcast host than a documentary narrator.

narratorStyles.label: Documentary deadpan
narratorStyles.description: Quiet, authoritative, almost reverent — Attenborough-meets-dark-comedy. Lets the writing do the work.

introDefaults.exampleText: Today on {channel_name}… why it sucks to be born as a {subject}. They look harmless. They aren't. Here are {chapter_count} reasons being one is a slow-motion disaster — starting with the most painful.

imagePrompts.purposeNote: for a Bound-style 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' explainer (one hand-drawn cartoon scene per sentence-or-two, thick black outline, flat fills, curved arrow + handwritten caption labelling the hardship)
imagePrompts.visualStyleHint: Bound-channel cartoon style — thick uneven black outline, flat solid fills with minimal shading, single anthropomorphic-but-anatomically-accurate subject, hand-drawn curved arrow pointing to the feature being discussed, handwritten caption (3-6 words) next to the arrow
imagePrompts.defaultStyleTag: Bound / In The Black Media YouTube channel cartoon style: thick uneven black ink outline, flat solid color fills with minimal cel-shading, single anatomically-accurate-but-anthropomorphic subject (one face, exaggerated eyes), simple solid-color or pale-gradient background. Add ONE hand-drawn curved arrow (rough freehand line, not a vector) pointing to the specific anatomical feature or behavior being discussed. Add ONE handwritten caption (3-6 words, marker-style hand lettering, slight slant) next to the arrow, summarizing the hardship in present-tense fragment style ('Can't Control Its Face Weapon', 'Sprays Acid From Body', 'Drinks Blood Of Bigger Birds'). Aspect 16:9, subject takes 50-70% of frame, arrow + caption occupy the negative space.

metadata.purposeNote: for a 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' explainer episode about one specific species
metadata.titleStyleHint: Always 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As a [Subject]' — no variations, no subtitles, no colons. The formula IS the brand.
titleHookRules: Title formula is locked: 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As a [Subject]'. Variations like 'Reasons It's Bad To Be A [Subject]' are off-brand.
Subject name is always specific (single species, e.g. 'Komodo Dragon', 'Venus Flytrap'), capitalized as a proper noun.
Keep under 60 chars where possible so the title doesn't truncate in mobile previews.

Include the niche tags (plants / animals / fungi / insects, depending on subject).

productionStandardsAddendum:
BOUND-STYLE EXPLAINER FORMAT — CRITICAL RULES

1. Title formula is locked: 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As a [Subject]'. Never improvise on the title shape.
2. Subject is always ONE specific species. Categories ('plants', 'big cats') belong to a different format.
3. Each chapter is one concrete, evidence-based hardship — anatomical, ecological, behavioral, or reproductive.
4. Each chapter opens with the bluntest possible hook sentence and ends with a dry one-liner. No PSA closers.
5. Cite biology — mechanism, evidence, comparison. Bare assertions kill credibility.
6. Sentences are SHORT (10-20 words). The cartoon swaps every 3-6 seconds, so each sentence must map cleanly to one visual.
7. Banned vocabulary: 'mind-blowing', 'shocking', 'tragic', 'heartbreaking', 'devastating'. The humor lands when biology is stated flat, not when sold.
8. Image prompts ALWAYS include: thick black outline, flat fills, single subject, ONE curved arrow, ONE handwritten caption. Never deviate from the visual signature.
